title: Note Taking Apps Comparison for 2026
description: A side-by-side comparison of popular note taking applications — Notion, Evernote, Obsidian, Roam Research, and Apple Notes — evaluating features, organization methods, and collaboration capabilities.
body:
Note taking applications have evolved from simple text editors to comprehensive knowledge management platforms. Modern note taking apps support rich media, database organization, bidirectional linking, and team collaboration.

This comparison evaluates five note taking applications across the dimensions that matter most: organization methods, search capabilities, cross-platform availability, collaboration features, and export options. Pricing references should be verified against each vendor's current rates.

## Notion

Notion combines note taking with database functionality, project management, and wiki capabilities. Its flexible block-based editor supports text, tables, databases, kanban boards, calendars, and embedded content within a single workspace.

Notion's organization model uses nested pages that can contain databases, making it powerful for both personal knowledge management and team documentation. The template gallery provides pre-built workspaces for common use cases.

Notion's free plan provides generous personal use capabilities. Paid plans add version history, unlimited storage, and team collaboration features.

Check Notion's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Evernote

Evernote is the most established dedicated note taking application, known for its notebook and tag organization system and powerful search capabilities. The platform supports text notes, document scanning, web clipping, and audio notes.

Evernote's search capabilities remain best in class, including search within attached documents and images. The web clipper browser extension captures full web pages, articles, and screenshots for offline reference.

Evernote's free plan is limited to two devices. Paid plans remove device restrictions, add offline access, and increase attachment size limits.

Check Evernote's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Obsidian

Obsidian is a local-first note taking application that uses plain Markdown files stored on the user's device. Its unique value proposition is privacy, longevity, and extensibility through a plugin ecosystem.

Obsidian's bidirectional linking creates a knowledge graph that visualizes connections between notes. The graph view reveals patterns and relationships that are invisible in traditional folder-based organization. The plugin marketplace extends functionality with community-developed plugins.

Obsidian is free for personal use. Paid plans provide sync across devices, publish functionality, and commercial licensing.

Check Obsidian's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Roam Research

Roam Research pioneered the outliner-based note taking approach with bidirectional linking and block-level referencing. Its unique structure enables organic knowledge development where notes grow and connect over time.

Roam's block-level referencing allows any block of text to be referenced from any other note, creating a web of interconnected knowledge that grows more valuable over time. Daily notes serve as the default entry point, with pages created as needed.

Roam Research uses a subscription pricing model. A free plan with limited functionality is available. Paid plans include unlimited blocks, file uploads, and collaboration features.

Check Roam Research's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Apple Notes

Apple Notes is the default note taking application for Apple device users. Its tight integration with the Apple ecosystem provides seamless syncing across iPhone, iPad, and Mac devices with no additional software cost.

Apple Notes supports rich text, sketches, scanned documents, tables, and collaborative editing. The quick note feature enables note creation from any application using a keyboard shortcut or trackpad gesture.

Apple Notes is free for all Apple device users. Its limitations include limited organization options, no cross-platform support for Windows or Android, and no web access.

## Selection Guidance

The right note taking application depends on organizational style, collaboration needs, and platform preferences. Notion is best for users who want databases and project management alongside notes. Evernote excels for research-intensive users with powerful search requirements. Obsidian suits privacy-conscious users who want local-first, extensible note taking. Roam Research serves knowledge workers who benefit from bidirectional linking and daily notes. Apple Notes is ideal for Apple-exclusive users who want a free, integrated solution.
